gotchas.text: The address is 0x3C or 0x3D (the jumper on the back). A board printed “0x78” is 0x3C: the print shows the address shifted left by one bit.

gotchas.text: A 128×64 display needs a 1 KB screen buffer in RAM. On a board with 2 KB of RAM (Uno, Nano) that leaves little for the rest of the sketch.

source.title: Adafruit SSD1306 library
source.section: Buffer of width × height / 8 bytes; ATmega328P datasheet: 2 KB SRAM

registers.note: The SSD1306 is driven by commands. Only the status byte can be read back; the command table shows what each command does, not what the chip is set to now. Every I2C write starts with a control byte: 0x00 means commands follow, 0x40 means pixel data follows.

registers.name: status
registers.text: Status byte. The app sends the control byte 0x00 (commands follow, but none is sent), then reads one byte.

fields.name: ON/OFF
fields.text: Whether the display is switched on.

values.1: Display OFF (sleep mode). Your code must send 0xAF to switch it on.

source.title: Solomon Systech SSD1306 datasheet
source.section: 8.1 MCU interface: read status byte (D6 = display ON/OFF); 8.1.5.1 control byte

commands.name: Set contrast
commands.text: Brightness from 0 to 255 (reset 0x7F).

commands.name: Entire display ON
commands.text: 0xA4 shows the picture in memory; 0xA5 lights every pixel (a quick test).

commands.name: Normal / inverse
commands.text: 0xA6 normal; 0xA7 swaps lit and dark pixels.

commands.name: Display OFF / ON
commands.text: 0xAE switches the display off (sleep, the reset state); 0xAF switches it on.

commands.name: Horizontal scroll setup
commands.text: Sets up scrolling to the right (0x26) or left (0x27).

commands.name: Stop / start scroll
commands.text: 0x2E stops scrolling; 0x2F starts it.

commands.name: Lower column start
commands.text: Low 4 bits of the start column (page addressing mode).

commands.name: Higher column start
commands.text: High 4 bits of the start column (page addressing mode).

commands.name: Memory addressing mode
commands.text: 0 horizontal, 1 vertical, 2 page (the reset state).

commands.name: Column address
commands.text: First and last column written (horizontal or vertical mode).

commands.name: Page address
commands.text: First and last page written (horizontal or vertical mode).

commands.name: Page start
commands.text: Picks the page (a band of 8 pixel rows) to write in page addressing mode.

commands.name: Display start line
commands.text: Which memory row is shown at the top of the screen.

commands.name: Segment re-map
commands.text: Mirrors the picture left to right.

commands.name: Multiplex ratio
commands.text: Number of rows driven, minus one: 63 for 128×64, 31 for 128×32.

commands.name: COM scan direction
commands.text: 0xC0 or 0xC8: flips the picture upside down.

commands.name: Display offset
commands.text: Shifts the picture up or down by rows.

commands.name: COM pins configuration
commands.text: Must match the module's wiring: 0x12 on most 128×64 modules, 0x02 on 128×32. A wrong value shows every other line.

commands.name: Clock divide / oscillator
commands.text: Display clock: sets the refresh rate.

commands.name: No operation
commands.text: Does nothing.

commands.name: Charge pump
commands.text: 0x14 turns the built-in charge pump on, 0x10 off. Most modules need it on before 0xAF, or the screen stays dark.
